item.title: The Quest for the Aryan Eden: Reclaiming Our Hidden Heritage
item.description: Type: Tome Category: TomesLanguage: English Author: Leopold Fontanelle Date: 1932 A survey of often contradictory theories concerning lost civilizations, including subterranean ones. Focuses on locating the ancestral homeland of the so-called Aryan people and unlocking the power therein, concentrating on the polar regions and referencing various legends of Hyperborea, Thule, and Lomar. The book can be ordered from Hitherne Press or found in bookstores carrying esoteric materials.Back to Shared Tomes
item.guid: 19 Player Publish/Shared Library/Tomes/The Quest for the Aryan Eden Reclaiming Our Hidden Heritage.md

item.description:

The precursor Pnakotica was written in classical Greek and may preserve knowledge originating with prehuman crinoid beings.Chant - of - ThothCall of Cthulhu, “Tomes of Eldritch Lore,” page(s) 233 in the supplied PDF.

item.title: Ancient Roman Pnakotic Scroll
item.description: Type: Tome Category: TomesLanguage: Latin Author and translator: Unknown Date: c. 200 BCE This scroll claims to be a translation from an Etruscan stone tablet. It discusses the crystals of Naphkon, which the ancient Lomarians considered sacred, and details how to create them. The Lomarians used the stones to view distant times, places, and worlds. They could project their psyches—or even those of others—through these stones. A “Great Race” was credited with creating and truly mastering such projection techniques.Back to Shared Tomes
item.guid: 19 Player Publish/Shared Library/Tomes/Ancient Roman Pnakotic Scroll.md

item.title: Chant of Thoth
item.description: Type: Spell Category: spells 10 magic points; 1D4 Sanity points. 30 minutes The use of this spell increases the caster’s mental faculties, boosting his or her chance of solving a particular intellectual problem. Spending 10 magic points in the chant grants the caster a bonus die on his or her dice roll to gain knowledge, learn a spell, translate a passage, deduce the meaning of a symbol, etc.The Rite of Cerebral Acuity, The Song of Erudite Addition, The Scholars Chorus. Dismiss Deity Spell Names When composing alternative names for Dismiss Deity spells, consider the following words for inspiration: Banishment Repel Repudiate Dispel Bane Cast Out Exile Evict Also, try to use evocative and subtle names for the actual Mythos deities rather than simply using their common names. There’s no reason why a spell name concerning Yog-Sothoth couldn’t reference the being as The Hideous Spheres, or The Unquenchable Thirster of Souls, and so forth. Keeping the players guessing about what a spell will do or to whom it’s connected can help to stimulate mystery and fear of the unknown. Cthugha has 210 POW and so 8 magic points are needed to ‘open the way’ to dismiss this monstrosity. 8 magic points opens the way for Cthugha, representing a 5% chance for dismissal. Sacrificing 10 more magic points increases the chance to 55%. To have a 99% (the maximum achievable) chance of dismissing Cthugha, those assembled must sacrifice 8+19 magic points in the two stages, a total of 27 magic points. Harvey is trying to translate a Latin scroll. He casts Chant of Thoth, spending 10 magic points. He has a Latin skill of 66. He rolls 84 and 34 (bonus die); a success. The chant has expanded his mental capacities for a short time, during which he fully comprehends the Latin language.Back to Shared Spells

item.title: Heart of Dreams
item.description: Type: Item Category: dreamlands-artifactHearts of Dreams are rare items, much sought after by those who know and understand their abilities. The hearts are known by different names; many have cultural associations or are related to the land of dream, and much myth and folklore surround them.One legend concerning the hearts seems to cross cultural boundaries and concerns the foul keepers or guardians of the hearts, who torment those who risk using a heart’s power without due deference to Hypnos, Lord of Dream.These strange devices usually take the form of a red crystalline cube run through with jagged lines of yellow material.A Heart of Dreams is used to view other places in dream. These places could include distant lands, planets, and other dimensions.Back to Shared Items

item.title: Crystal of Naphkon
item.description: Type: Item Category: item Chapter: Chapter 1To fashion a crystal of Naphkon requires a large amethyst, which can be easily purchased in New York City for $20 for a rough, poor quality stone. Higher quality stones cost $50 to $100+.See Create Crystal of Naphkon, page 161.Once created, the crystal may be used to home in on the kidnapped psyches.A character may activate the crystal with either: A successful Clairvoyance roll and 1D6+1 magic points, or A successful Psychometry roll and 1D6+1 magic points if touching a possession of one of the victims, such as bedding or an empty bottle from the cellar. Without psychic talents, activation requires: A successful Hard POW roll, and 1D8+5 magic points. The process is similar to viewing different times and places, but the costs and process are slightly different due to the psychic turmoil caused by this event.The vision reveals six men and women trapped in an unfurnished room with marble floors and walls. All of them are wearing amethyst necklaces. They are dressed in loose tunics, and the men have forked beards.One is frantically pounding on the door, while others pace or slump dejectedly. There is one tall, thin window, too narrow to squeeze through.Suddenly, all of the inhabitants react, apparently to sounds outside. One of them runs to the window and looks down. The viewer now sees that they are in a high tower.Down below, flames are spreading through a partly ruined city, and tunic-clad, gray-eyed people are fighting shaggy umber-colored humanoids. A six-legged, white-furred beast with a horn jutting from its head rampages past.The vision ends abruptly with a sense of impending doom for the victims.The experience costs the viewer 0/1D4 Sanity points.See Call of Cthulhu Rulebook, page 175 for Mythos tome ratings.Back to Shared Items

item.title: Pulp Luck Spending
item.description: Category: pulpPulp Cthulhu – Luck‑Spend Options (Quick‑Reference Table) Luck Cost is expressed in the amount of Luck points that must be spent from the character’s (or NPC’s) Luck pool. When a rule says “all Luck points,” the entire remaining pool is consumed. Identify the situation (e.g., you just failed a Sanity roll, or you’re about to die). Find the matching row to see what the Luck spend accomplishes. Check the cost and verify you have enough Luck points. Declare the spend to the Keeper; apply the effect immediately. Feel free to adapt or house‑rule any of these options to suit the tone of your campaign!Back to Pulp Rules

item.title: Pulp Combat Damage
item.description: Category: combat Natural Healing – +2 HP per day (Quick Healer talent bumps this to +3 HP/day). First Aid / Medicine Boost – Successful rolls heal +1D4 HP (Extreme success = 4 HP). No Major‑Wound Penalty – Heroes do not suffer the usual major‑wound effects. Death Thresholds Instant death: Single attack ≥ maximum HP. Dying: Single attack ≥ ½ maximum HP and reduces HP to 0. Unconscious: HP drops to 0 (but not ≥ ½ max). Half‑HP Shock: If a single blow cuts HP by ≥ ½ max and leaves the hero above 0, they must make a CON roll to stay conscious. Dying State – Mark current HP as “D” (dying). CON Rolls – Made at the end of each round; any failure = immediate death. Stabilizing First Aid (success) → removes “D”, restores 1D4 HP (Extreme = 4 HP). Extreme Cases (e.g., being ripped apart) may render First Aid impossible – death is inevitable. Follow‑up Medicine – After stabilization, a successful Medicine roll adds another 1D4 HP (Extreme = 4 HP). Base Rate – +2 HP/day (or +3 HP/day with Quick Healer). Medical Assistance – Each successful daily Medicine roll adds 1 HP to that day’s natural healing (total +3 HP). Modifiers – Hospital care may grant a bonus die; unsanitary conditions may impose a penalty die. Failed Medicine – May reduce healing (e.g., lose 1 HP or, on a pushed roll, lose 1D3 HP). Near‑Death Trauma – Typically triggers a Sanity roll (0 or 1 SAN loss depending on outcome). Role‑Playing Hook – Encourage players to describe lingering injuries (broken limbs, missing fingers, etc.) for dramatic effect, but remember pulp heroes can often “brush it off.” Spending Luck – A dying hero may expend all remaining Luck points (minimum 30 LP required) to cheat death. Result of Luck Spend Luck drops to 0. Hero immediately regains 1D6 + 1 HP. Injuries remain; further healing still required. No further CON rolls needed for that death episode. Narrative Requirement – Player must describe how the hero miraculously survives. Max HP = 22, current = 8. Trap deals 18 damage → HP = ‑10 → Dying (≥ ½ max, reduced to 0). First Aid succeeds → “D” removed, 1D4 HP restored (e.g., 3 HP). Medicine roll succeeds → additional 1D4 HP (e.g., 4 HP). Natural healing resumes (+2 HP/day, possibly +1 HP from daily Medicine). Max HP = 34, current = 17. Star‑spawn claw deals 19 damage → HP = ‑2 → Dying (≥ ½ max, reduced to 0). Luck spend (≥ 30 LP) → Luck → 0, regain 1D6 + 1 HP (e.g., 5 HP). CON roll at end of round succeeds → remains conscious. Allies apply First Aid (success) → +1D4 HP (e.g., 3 HP). Daily Medicine rolls add extra HP each day (+1 HP per successful roll). Facing instant death from Cthulhu’s foot, Maximillian spends all 36 Luck (≥ 30). Describes a cinematic survival (e.g., diving behind a shattered column, a gust of wind lifting him). Luck drops to 0, he regains 1D6 + 1 HP, avoids death, and continues the chase. Back to Pulp Rules

item.title: Cthulhu Mythos (Pulp Spontaneous Magic)
item.description: Category: skillsPlayer states an aim; Keeper may suggest a weaker one. Default difficulty = Regular (roll ≤ Cthulhu Mythos). When affecting a resisting target, treat as an opposed roll Cthulhu Mythos vs POW.Physical harm: Spend MP, lose half that amount of SAN; on a successful opposed roll the target takes damage equal to MP spent (horrific effects). Banish monster: Pay MP = ⅕ × monster POW + 1D4 SAN; succeed on opposed roll to banish. Communion with the dead: Recent dead - 10 MP + 1D10 SAN, lasts 1D6 rounds. Long‑term dead - 15 MP + 1D10 SAN, lasts 1D4 rounds. Physical ward: Variable MP/SAN; each MP adds one point of armor (no protection vs. mental/psychic attacks). Understand Mythos languages: 8 MP + 1D6 SAN; comprehension lasts ~1 hour.Back to Skills Rules
